title: VERTICO V: The environmentally driven evolution of the inner cold gas discs of Virgo cluster galaxies
question: How do cluster environmental mechanisms impact the surviving atomic and molecular gas in the inner optical discs of Virgo cluster galaxies on 1.2-kpc scales?

recipe.goal: Select galaxy samples and homogenise spatial resolution and pixel grids
recipe.method: Select massive (log(M_*/M_sun) >= 10), moderately inclined (i <= 70 deg) galaxies from VERTICO (excluding NGC 4772 and NGC 4698) and star-forming control galaxies from HERACLES/THINGS. Smooth CO(2-1) and H I cubes with CASA IMSMOOTH to match a 1200 pc physical beam and 650 pc spaxel size (15 arcsec beam, 8 arcsec spaxels at Virgo).
key_parameters: log(M_*/M_sun) >= 10, i <= 70 deg, physical resolution = 1200 pc, spaxel size = 650 pc
assumptions: Virgo distance = 16.5 Mpc; Kroupa (2001) IMF; LambdaCDM cosmology with h = 0.7, Omega_M = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7

recipe.goal: Compute spatially resolved surface densities (Sigma_HI, Sigma_mol, Sigma_*) and mask to optical disc
recipe.method: Apply signal masks to create moment 0 maps; convert integrated fluxes to H I mass (Eq. 1), CO luminosity (Eq. 2), and molecular gas mass (Eq. 3); compute WISE pixel-by-pixel stellar mass; divide by 650-pc pixel area; de-project by cos(i); and mask spaxels to within B-band R_25.
key_parameters: R_21 = 0.8, alpha_CO = 4.35 M_sun pc^-2, intrinsic axial ratio q = 0.2
assumptions: Optically thin H I emission; no Helium correction for H I in Sections 2-4 (36% Helium included in alpha_CO, and 36% Helium added to H I in Section 5)

recipe.goal: Determine H I deficiency categories and H I truncation radius stellar surface density (<log Sigma_*>_HI)
recipe.method: Calculate def-H I from Eq. 4 and split VERTICO H I-deficient galaxies into moderate (def-H I = [0.3, 0.7) dex) and large (def-H I >= 0.7 dex) subsamples. Compute radial profiles of log Sigma_HI and log Sigma_* in 4-arcsec annuli to find R_HI where radial average Sigma_HI = 1 M_sun pc^-2, and record the average log Sigma_* at R_HI (<log Sigma_*>_HI).
key_parameters: 4-arcsec annuli; Sigma_HI(R_HI) = 1 M_sun pc^-2; def-H I bins: [0.3, 0.7) dex and >= 0.7 dex

recipe.goal: Construct galaxy-weighted resolved scaling relations and distributions in bins of Sigma_* and within R_HI
recipe.method: Weight each spaxel by 1/(N_sp * N_G) so each galaxy contributes equally. Compute density-normalised histograms and weighted medians/percentiles of log Sigma_HI and log Sigma_mol in 0.5 dex bins of log Sigma_* and for spaxels within R_HI (log Sigma_* >= <log Sigma_*>_HI), constructing matched control samples for the R_HI comparison.
key_parameters: log Sigma_* bins: [0, 0.75), [0.75, 1.25), [1.25, 1.75), [1.75, 2.25), >= 2.25; non-detections set to log Sigma = -0.5; quantitative Sigma_mol comparisons restricted to log Sigma_* >= 1.25

recipe.goal: Test physical drivers of molecular gas reduction using Sigma_mol / Sigma_HI vs ISM condition proxies and mock H I-stripped galaxies
recipe.method: For detected spaxels with log Sigma_* >= 1.25 (including 36% Helium in H I), compare log(Sigma_mol/Sigma_HI) against midplane hydrostatic pressure proxy Sigma_*^0.5 * Sigma_gas and total gas surface density Sigma_gas. Create mock H I-stripped control galaxies by subtracting the median log Sigma_HI offset of each VERTICO galaxy at fixed Sigma_* from HERACLES spaxels, and compare observed distributions to mock H I-only removal predictions.
key_parameters: log(Sigma_*^0.5 * Sigma_gas) bins: [1.5, 2.0) and [2.0, 2.5); log(Sigma_gas) bins: [0.85, 1.35) and [1.35, 1.85); log Sigma_* >= 1.25
assumptions: 36 per cent Helium contribution added to H I masses; stellar scale height and gas velocity dispersion have minor contributions to midplane pressure.

score_reason: The VERTICO CO(2-1) cubes/maps are publicly hosted on CANFAR, HERACLES/THINGS/WISE data are public, sample selection and equations/conversions are completely specified, numeric summary tables (Tables 1-3) are provided, and the custom weighted K-S test code is linked on GitHub. Only the custom re-imaged VIVA H I maps and the end-to-end spaxel-matching pipeline scripts are not directly hosted.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA ACA survey products (VERTICO on CANFAR) and well-defined mathematical recipes for converting moment-0 maps to de-projected surface densities and galaxy-weighted medians make the main numeric results in Tables 2 and 3 strong candidates for reproduction.
